title: Lead with creator-specific positioning instead of generic Mac care
rationale: The headlines observed are broad: CleanMyMac says "Smart & effortless Mac care", Sensei says "The All-in-One Mac System Performance Monitoring Tool", and MacCleaner Pro says "A bundle of six professional tools for a deep Mac cleanup". CacheDrop can name its audience of music producers, developers and video editors and speak to their caches, plug-ins and leftovers. This is a messaging choice, not a claim that no one serves these users.

title: Make plug-in management a headline feature for music producers
rationale: MacCleaner Pro is the only observed product with plug-in management confirmed, and it is one of six tools in a bundle. CacheDrop can make plug-in management the centerpiece of the producer story, with depth and workflow fit as the proof, rather than one item in a list.

title: Pair developer-cache cleanup with uninstall and disk analysis in one one-time purchase
rationale: Mole shows that developer cleanup, uninstall, cleanup and a disk map can be sold together as a one-time $19 direct purchase, and its headline stresses developer and AI data. CacheDrop can compete for developers by also covering producer and video-editor workflows in the same license. Price and scope need testing against this reference point.

title: Use the one-time price as a clear contrast with subscription-style options, and justify it with breadth
rationale: Observed one-time prices range from DaisyDisk at $9.99 and Mole at $19 to Sensei at $59 and MacCleaner Pro at $85.95. Sensei and MacCleaner Pro also list annual prices of $29 and $39.95. Single-purpose tools sit at the low end and broader suites at the high end. CacheDrop should price according to the breadth it delivers (cleanup, uninstall and plug-in management) and state plainly that the purchase is one-time with no renewal.

title: Offer a trial with clearly stated terms and no credit card
rationale: DaisyDisk offers an untimed trial with some features locked and no credit card. MacCleaner Pro gives a 2-day full-access Pro trial with no credit card. CleanMyMac offers a trial but does not state its terms. CacheDrop can stand out with explicit trial terms and no card, letting creators test it on their own plug-in and cache libraries before buying.
